business_scope.primary_industry_name: Security Holographic Cold Foil Printing of Collectible Trading Cards

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified under the French Commercial Code and Civil Code; AML/CFT codified under the French Monetary and Financial Code)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (2009, in force 2010)
France–China Agreement for the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (1985)
France–Hong Kong Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital Gains (2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, arts. L.561-1, L.561-2-1, R.561-1 et seq. (as amended by Loi no. 2016-731 'Sapin II'); Code de commerce, arts. L.123-3 and R.123-54 (UBO declaration to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); Décret no. 2017-497 of 6 April 2017; EU Directives 2015/849 and 2018/843 (4AMLD/5AMLD).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official corporate extract or certificate of good standing/company registration certificate of any corporate shareholder holding 25% or more of the SAS capital or voting rights
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or commercial register in the shareholder/UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization by the French embassy if the source state is not an Apostille-Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the identification passport or national ID of each natural-person UBO and legal representative (president/directors of the SAS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly licensed notary public in the country of origin or the competent national authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and legal representative (utility bill, bank statement, or notarized affidavit), issued within the last 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original document plus sworn/certified French translation; notarization and apostille/consularization if requested by the Registration Registrar or AML officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, legal representatives, directors, and senior officers against (i) French national financial sanctions and provisional asset-freeze lists maintained by ACPR/Tracfin; (ii) EU consolidated restrictive-measures lists (Common Foreign and Security Policy; Reg. (EC) No 881/2002 and Reg. (EU) No 2580/2001); (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) OFAC SDN list for all USD-denominated transactions, particularly due to the planned use of Stripe and Authorize.Net payment clearing rails; and (v) PEP databases (category A/B/C) under Code monétaire et financier arts. L.561-6 and L.561-6-1. Enhanced due diligence is automatically triggered if any UBO is a PEP, is resident in a FATF-identified high-risk/non-cooperative jurisdiction, or matches a sanctions red flag.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); RCS records and name availability verified through INPI/Infogreffe repositories.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS corporate name (dénomination sociale) may be in French or in another language, but must be written in Latin script. Names in non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into Latin characters. Every incorporation application and all foreign-language supporting documents must be accompanied by a French translation prepared by a sworn or expert translator admitted by a French Court of Appeal. The official statutes must state the full corporate powers and the suffix 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or its abbreviation 'SAS'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: FINANCE / ASSURANCE / CRÉDIT (regulated financial terms requiring prior specific licence)
PRÉSIDENT / MAIRE / MINISTÈRE / GENDARMERIE / POLICE (official positions/state institutions)
UNIVERSITÉ / ACADÉMIE (academic titles requiring State/ministry authorization)
CHAMBRE DE COMMERCE / BOURSE (institutional names requiring ministerial or professional body approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection by the INPI registrar will be notified in the Guichet unique portal. The applicant has 15 days to submit a corrected name without a new registration fee. If the rejection relies on an earlier trademark or trade-name opposition, the applicant may contest the opposition before the INPI Director (for trademarks) or before the competent Tribunal judiciaire (for unfair competition). If the registrar itself refuses the application on formal legal grounds, an administrative/hierarchical appeal may be lodged with the INPI, and a judicial appeal lies with the President of the Tribunal de commerce in the company's registered-office jurisdiction under Article L.123-3 of the Code de commerce. Emergency interim relief is available via the référé procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible but constrained. An SAS may register at a commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under applicable French Commercial Code provisions, provided a written domiciliation agreement, a physical address in France, mail reception facilities and a local supervision obligation exist. For a trading-cards publishing/holographic print company, a purely virtual office with no French management, personnel, or records is not prudent; it may create a permanent-establishment, substance, and VAT-avoidance risk and would invite closer investigation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk, estimated at 5-10% annual probability for a low-risk/standard AML-CFT tier; however, unannounced on-site inspections are legally possible where substance indicators are inadequate or where a tax audit or AML red flag is raised (Code de commerce articles L.123-12-1 and Livre des procédures fiscales article L.13).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II, Chapter VII, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general formation rules under Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; implementing decrees R.227-1 to R.227-3; incorporation formalities governed by the unified 'Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises' regime introduced by the 2021 French single-window reform.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI – Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), transmitting to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce territorialement compétent for the registered office (in Paris: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris), which maintains the RCS file and issues the K-bis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic 'Déclaration de constitution de société' (replacing the historical M0 form) submitted via the Guichet unique, together with the fully executed Statuts (Articles of Association) and all statutorily annexed certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital: the amount is freely fixed in the Statuts (Eur 1,000 is commonly adopted for commercial credibility). Cash contributions must be paid up to at least 50% of nominal value before registration, with the balance due within five years. Subscription funds must be deposited in a blocked account with a French bank, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and are released only against the RCS registration certificate (K-bis).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [SAS NAME], SAS, dated [DATE]: under Articles L.227-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code, the sole shareholder resolves: (1) to approve the final Articles of Association; (2) to subscribe in full the issued capital of EUR [AMOUNT] represented by [NUMBER] ordinary shares; (3) to adopt the registered office at [ADDRESS] within the jurisdiction of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de [CITY]; (4) to appoint [NAME] as President, with all powers under Article L.227-6; (5) to appoint [AUDITOR NAME] as statutory auditor, if required; and (6) to authorize the President to deposit subscription funds, publish the legal notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales, complete filings via the Guichet unique, and open the corporate bank account. Certified true copy of the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-validation of Company Name, Corporate Object and Execution of Statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or notary (optional) using the Infogreffe company-name database; INSEE NAF typology code 32.40Z
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify name availability and absence of prior trademarks in the relevant classes; confirm that the corporate object covers the design, security holographic cold-foil printing, manufacture and distribution of collectible trading cards; draft the Statuts with prescribed legal content (form, name, duration, capital, registered office, object, governance of the President, share transfer rules and decision-making procedures); have all shareholders sign the Statuts and initial the share-subscription list.
required_dossiers: Share-subscription list annexed to the Statuts
Domiciliation agreement or proof of ownership of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or the object is deficient, revise the draft with a sleep alternate name and reformulated object clause; no registry fee is forfeited at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Deposit of Share Capital and Publication of the Legal Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for the capital deposit; authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) for the statutory notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account in the name of the company in formation, transfer the subscribed cash contributions, and obtain the bank's blocked-funds certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds). Concurrently, place the mandatory incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal gazette stating name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate object and filing registry, and collect the attestation de parution.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening file (company name, Statuts draft, UBO forms)
Proof of transfer of share capital
Blocked-funds certificate issued by the bank or notary
JAL insertion form and publication attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues an AML query, supply a source-of-funds declaration and updated beneficial-ownership statement; alternatively, re-deposit the funds with a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations to obtain the required certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Dossier via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), acting on behalf of the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Guichet unique, complete the electronic incorporation declaration (previous M0 form), upload the statutory annexes in PDF, apply the electronic signatures of the legal representative or proxy, pay the registry fees online, and submit the dossier; the platform transmits the file to the competent registry and issues an acknowledgement of receipt or a reasoned notice of incompleteness.
required_dossiers: Identity document and declaration of honour of the President
Power of attorney, if filing through a proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet notifies incompleteness, rectification must be made online within the legal cure period; if the delay expires, the applicant may refile the full dossier and, in contested cases, petition the registry judge (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) for restitution of the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of the K-bis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris (or of the department where the registered office is located)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the complete dossier, the registry records the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, assigns SIREN/SIRET identification numbers, and issues the Extrait K-bis, which is the sole legal proof of existence of the company; the registry simultaneously transmits the data to INSEE, URSSAF, the tax administration (DGFiP) and the Répertoire National des Entreprises (RNE).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry fees
Any rectification documents requested by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of refusal, the registry must issue a reasoned decision; an appeal may be lodged with the judge of the commercial court within 15 days; clerical errors in the K-bis are corrected on application to the Greffe with no further judicial step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Administrative Activation (Tax, Social and Economic Identifiers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP (tax), URSSAF (social), INSEE (statistical identifiers) and optionally CCI Paris Île-de-France
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify automatic generation of the VAT identification number, SIRET and URSSAF registration number through the Guichet unique account; download the official attestations; release the blocked capital through the K-bis; activate the corporate bank account; register for the cotisation foncière des entreprises (CFE); and notify the occupational health service before the first employee is hired.
required_dossiers: President's compensation statement and CIPAV/URSSAF status declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an identifier is missing, file a corrective message via the Guichet unique; in case of persistent error, contact the INPI RNE monitoring service for rectification or apply directly to the competent Greffe for correction of the RCS entry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Préfecture du département (ICPE declaration or registration under Code de l'environnement) supported by DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement); occupational safety and workplace control exercised by DREETS/DRIEETS (Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing permit is required for the printing and publishing of collectible trading cards under French law; a regulated environmental filing (ICPE declaration or registration under Rubrique 2450 of the nomenclature des installations classées) applies only if the installation's organic-solvent consumption from inks, varnishes, adhesives or cleaning agents reaches the regulatory thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement, under Articles L.122-1 et seq. and R.512-1 et seq. of the French Code de l'environnement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Case-by-case screening (examen au cas par cas) is required for installations listed under the ICPE regime; a full French EIA report is generally not mandatory for a small holographic cold-foil printing unit unless the site meets the higher solvent-usage thresholds of ICPE Rubrique 2450 or is located in a protected natural or urban sensitivity zone where the prefect may impose a full impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The installation must comply with EU Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions (including VOC management plans and exhaust-abatement measures for solvent-based processes); wastewater discharged into the municipal sewer must respect local discharge limits (commonly pH 5.5 to 9.5, TSS below 600 mg/l, COD below 2,000 mg/l); hazardous wastes (solvent residues, ink waste, foil scrap) must be traced through the bordereau de suivi des déchets (BSD) and disposed of by registered waste contractors; packaging placed on the French market triggers extended producer-responsibility (REP) obligations under the AGEC law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Prior to operation the company must secure: (i) building legality certification against the local urban-planning code (production of the building permit or prior-notification attestation to the Mairie); (ii) fire-safety conformity with the Règlement de sécurité contre l'incendie and the Labor Code, covering emergency exits, fire extinguishers, alarm systems and storage of flammable inks and foils in a dedicated flammable-liquid cabinet; (iii) a workplace health-and-safety clearance comprising the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUER) and the roll-out of occupational-health medical surveillance for the President and all employees; and (iv) where visitors have access, compliance of the premises with applicable ERP fire-safety classifications. No separate civil-defense license is mandated for this activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique – Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); official portals are impots.gouv.fr and guichet-unique.entreprises.gouv.fr (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An SAS formed under French law is first registered through the INPI guichet unique, which generates the SIREN/SIRET identifiers and the APE/NAF code at the Registre National des Entreprises. The company then applies to its territorial SIE on form 1603-SD before undertaking taxable transactions in order to obtain the French intra-Community VAT number. A foreign entity without a French establishment that makes taxable supplies in France registers directly with DGFIP/SIE using the same form 1603-SD; a non-EU-established taxable person generally must appoint an accredited French tax representative (représentant fiscal) under CGI Article 289-A. The registration application must include constitutional documents, proof of foreign establishment, a power of attorney and a description of the intended French economic activity. An EU seller may instead use the One Stop Shop for qualifying distance sales of goods, but any taxable activity requiring a localized French VAT identity requires the 1603-SD procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a French-resident SAS is a separate taxable person subject by default to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) on its profits; no pass-through default applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not have a US-style check-the-box election. Relevant elections for an SAS and French groups include: (i) election for fiscal integration (régime d'intégration fiscale) by a 95%-owned French group; (ii) option for a single VAT taxable person grouping (assujettissement unique) for closely linked entities; (iii) application to DGFIP for a different accounting/fiscal year end; and (iv) the parent-subsidiary regime (régime mère-fille) for dividend exemption where applicable. Hybrid and reverse-hybrid outcomes are governed by mandatory anti-hybrid rules implementing ATAD; there is no elective hybrid mismatch check-the-box item, and reportable cross-border arrangements must be disclosed under DAC6.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable to a French-established SAS: VAT registration and filing are compulsory from inception and from the first taxable transaction. For non-established EU sellers of goods to French consumers, the EU-wide distance-selling threshold of EUR 10,000 applies; taxable persons already established in France cannot use that threshold. Non-EU sellers must register before making any taxable French supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting. From 1 September 2026 all established taxable persons must be able to receive electronic invoices and large/medium enterprises must issue them; from 1 September 2027 all businesses, including SMEs/micro-enterprises, must issue electronic invoices and transmit transaction and payment data. Invoices must be issued in an EN 16931-conformant structured format (Factur-X, UBL or CII) and exchanged through a certified dematerialization partner (PDP) or the DGFIP public portal (PPF) in the 4-corner model. Transaction and payment data are reported to DGFIP through the PPF/PDP API. France does not presently operate a real-time inline fiscal stamp or clearance engine; no digital stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical export of collectible trading cards to a destination outside the EU is exempt from French VAT with credit for input VAT (effectively 0%) under CGI Articles 262-I-1° and 269, provided the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by or on behalf of the seller and the seller holds documentary proof of export. Directly connected services, such as packing, handling and shipping of the exported goods, may also be zero-rated under Article 262-I-2°. Services supplied to non-EU customers are outside the French VAT base under B2B place-of-supply rules (Article 259) when the customer is outside the EU. Intra-EU supplies of goods are not zero-rated but are exempt under Article 262-ter if the customer provides a valid EU VAT ID and the supplier files a recapitulative statement; e-commerce distance sales may fall under OSS/IOSS where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation/DAU) lodged through the DELTA-X/UX customs system with the export accompanying document
External transport evidence (Bill of Lading, CMR, Air Waybill, or postal/express consignment note showing dispatch outside the EU)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT MT103/bank credit advice evidencing receipt of the export proceeds
Proof of non-EU arrival/clearance where available (port release, customs entry, or signed proof of delivery copy)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are closely scrutinised by DGFIP during a vérification de comptabilité. If the exporter fails to produce the required customs, transport and payment evidence, or if the goods are diverted within the EU, the VAT becomes lawfully due and is clawed back with statutory late-payment interest and the 40% bad-faith penalty (manquement délibéré, CGI Article 1729) or the 80% penalty for fraudulent concealment (activité occulte), in addition to denial or reversal of input VAT credits and refunds. Criminal tax evasion under CGI Article 1741 can be prosecuted, carrying imprisonment up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000; legal representatives and directors may be jointly liable in cases of serious misconduct in managing the SAS.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), together with the Direction Générale du Trésor (Treasury) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; cross-border statistical reporting and balance-of-payments registration are administered by the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is part of the euro area and applies European capital movement rules. Current account and capital account transactions are broadly free of exchange controls for both residents and non-residents. The euro is fully convertible. Profit remittance requires no prior administrative authorization; dividends paid by a French SAS may be subject to withholding tax under national law (30% default) unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty or exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when paid to a qualifying EU parent. Outbound direct investment is unrestricted for EU counterparties; investment by non-EU parties in the collectible card printing sector (ISIC 3240) is not in the restricted sectors list and only requires ex post reporting to the Banque de France for statistical purposes. No exchange control approval is necessary for imports or exports of goods or for service payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not maintain mandatory export proceeds surrender or forced conversion timelines. Export receipts, whether in euros or foreign currencies, may be retained in commercial foreign currency accounts, converted freely at market rates, or repatriated without an obligatory deadline. However, for balance-of-payments statistics, French resident companies must declare direct investment and significant cross-border flows (including share capital and loans exceeding certain thresholds) to the Banque de France. The Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) requires truthful economic declarations for cross-border transfers, and funds from exports must be booked in accordance with standard invoice settlement timelines between related parties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte bloqué) and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Société Générale / Societe Generale Global Transaction Banking

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. / Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Treasury Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI (electronic money institution) accounts are legally viable in France when the provider is licensed by the ACPR or passporting under PSD2/EMD2 into France. Such accounts can support operational payments, collections, and FX conversion, and connect to SEPA, SWIFT, and card rails. However, EMIs are not suitable for the mandatory share-capital escrow account required before formation of a SAS, which must be held with a bank, a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. EMIs also typically cannot issue documentary credits (letters of credit) or provide committed credit facilities. Feasibility for transaction banking: Medium-High for collectible-card publishing collections and supplier payouts; Low for full treasury/liquidity clearing and trade finance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML legislation (Monetary and Financial Code Art. L.561-1 et seq.) permits customer identification by video or electronic means when the process satisfies specified authentication standards, and remote onboarding may be accepted for entities whose UBOs can be reliably identified. In practice, large French commercial banks often require an initial physical meeting of authorized signatories and, where relevant, beneficial owners, especially for non-resident directors, complex group structures, or opening an escrow/statutory capital account. A remote process is possible only if the bank accepts qualified electronic identification and all KYC documents are apostilled/certified; banks may still impose a physical branch visit for issues of bearer instruments or non-standard business models. The mandate is therefore bank-dependent: physical presence is de facto mandatory for most tier-1 facilities in the absence of an existing relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU or mixed beneficial ownership and opacity in the corporate structure of the French SAS
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart, statutory registration extracts (Kbis for French entity or equivalent), official register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), notarized or certified passports of UBOs, source of wealth documentation (tax returns, audited financial statements, bank references), and signed declaration confirming where applicable that no politically exposed person (PEP) is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model mismatch with banking parameters: high-value collectible trading cards combining holographic security printing, marketplace sales via Stripe/Authorize.Net, and physical exports to foreign distributors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, confirmed ISIC 3240 classification, any specialized licenses for security/holographic printing, supplier and customer lists, pro-forma invoices, distribution agreements, marketplace dashboard reports and settlement statements, export draft documents (Packing List, Commercial Invoice, Bill of Lading/Airway Bill), and completed sanctions/PEP screening outputs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound share capital injection or shareholder subordinated loan from a non-EU parent or third-country investor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement or loan agreement, corporate resolutions of the shareholder, full shareholder KYC file, bank reference letter from the remitting bank, proof of source of funds (asset realization statement, dividend records, audited accounts), tax identification numbers of the shareholder, and a copy of the ex post direct investment declaration to the Banque de France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments routed to or from tax-neutral, high-risk, or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions in the trading card supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic substance documentation, tax residency certificate, transfer pricing documentation when dealing with related parties, trade documents (contracts, invoices, Incoterms, customs declarations), due-diligence files on ultimate counterparties, and external screening confirmation showing no prohibited entity or jurisdiction involvement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial SAS share capital, funds must be deposited in a French bank blocked account (compte bloqué) or with a notary/share issue escrow. The transfer is initiated from the shareholder's bank by SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'G51' or equivalent equity-related code (e.g., outward direct investment by the sender's jurisdiction); for payments from within the EU, SEPA Transfer with regulation reference 'QUOS' may be used. French exchange control law does not require pre-authorization for non-resident equity investment in this hard-goods printing sector. After incorporation, the bank releases the credited amount to the business operating account on presentation of the registration certificate (Kbis). For ongoing capital contributions and loans, the routing should be via direct bank credit transfer with clear remittance narrative referencing the share capital or shareholder loan agreement; Banque de France balance-of-payments declarations (procedural 'DPU 1500' or the 'ex post' reporting) are required for direct investment flows above applicable thresholds or as otherwise instructed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to international suppliers and service providers are executed via SEPA for euro-denominated payments within the EEA, and via SWIFT MT103 for cross-border/foreign-currency payments. For large raw-material purchases or machinery imports from Asia, France-incorporated entities commonly use documentary collection or irrevocable letters of credit (commercial LC, MT700 issue/MT707 amendment, MT710/MT720 confirmations) issued through the corporate bank, particularly when the supplier requires title documents, bill of lading, packing list, commercial invoice, certificate of origin, and customs transit confirmation. Payment must include proper purpose codes/remittance references; for exports of trading cards to foreign distributors, receivables are collected via SEPA Direct Debit, card acquirers (Stripe/Authorize.Net), wire transfers, and bank drafts, with reconciliation by SWIFT notifications.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-fully-convertible currencies such as INR, CNY, and KRW, settled against published reference rates
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for multi-currency term debt
FX swaps and currency swaps for treasury liquidity management
Click-fix forwards and participating forwards, subject to the bank's credit line and eligibility assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or competent corporate approval body
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court injunction, director liability, and a civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and management report, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the competent Commercial Court (Greffe du tribunal de commerce), through the INPI one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months after approval when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and potential civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; persistent registry deficiencies may contribute to administrative removal procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and annual tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and penalties generally including 10% surcharge, with higher penalties possible for formal notices, concealment, or repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate local economic contribution compliance, including CFE information where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Service des impôts des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is generally assessed automatically; applicable declarations and payment follow the dates stated in the tax account, commonly with payment by 15 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and a generally applicable 5% late-payment surcharge, subject to tax administration enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI beneficial owner register and competent Commercial Court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership or controlling information; no routine annual filing where no change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, potential criminal liability for inaccurate or omitted information, and possible fines imposed on the legal representative and the entity

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Appointment of a statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Additional requirements may apply to qualifying groups, controlled entities, or upon a shareholder or court request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Chart of Accounts (Plan comptable général). IFRS is generally relevant to consolidated accounts of listed groups or where otherwise legally permitted or required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a routine annual UBO confirmation when previously filed information remains accurate. The SAS must update the beneficial owner filing within 30 days after any change in ownership, control, or identifying information. Share transfers must be documented in the share transfer register and reflected in shareholder records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or equivalent shareholder account records
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute book or secure register of shareholder and corporate decisions
Annual accounts approval and allocation-of-profit records
Beneficial owner filing evidence and supporting ownership documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,500 annually for commercial domiciliation or registered-office services; no registered agent is generally required under French law
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 2,000-8,000 annually for a small or medium SAS subject to statutory audit; complex or group audits may exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard CIT; 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit per full fiscal period for eligible SMEs with annual turnover below EUR 10 million
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT for SMEs; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% on eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% on eligible innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000 per year for SMEs; parent-subsidiary 95% exemption on qualifying dividends; carrying back deficits one year up to EUR 1,000,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward with no statutory expiry; annual offset restricted to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the remaining taxable profit for losses incurred before 2019, and with modified rules for recent years

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa n°2065-SD and annexed schedules 2050 to 2058-SD, together with the settlement form Cerfa n°2571-SD; filed via TéléIRI / EDI on impots.gouv.fr professional space; a non-resident SAS without a French establishment must appoint an accredited tax representative in France
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, filing due by 3 May of the following year (administrative practice); for any other closing date, the return must be lodged within three months of the fiscal year-end. Quarterly CIT advance payments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, and tax timing differences; positive amount equals taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only the taxable profit attributable to the French permanent establishment or French-source activity, determined under Article 209 CGI and OECD arm's length principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years to be offset against current year taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only carry forward losses realised through the same French permanent establishment or French-sourced taxable activity; foreign losses are not deductible unless attributable to the French business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 of 2065-SD (Impôt brut sur les sociétés)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at the statutory rate before application of credits and pre-payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard or reduced SME rate to French taxable income; treaty rate limitations do not apply to the levy of the French tax itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offsetting of research tax credit, innovation tax credit, foreign tax credits, and prepaid instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits permitted by French domestic law and applicable tax treaties; retain documentary support for any foreign tax credit with the tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance of corporate income tax payable after instalments and non-refundable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settlement must be made electronically; non-EU non-residents must use their French tax representative for payment and comply with the balance due deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 10% increase after the 30-day formal notice (mise en demeure), 40% increase where the return is knowingly inaccurate or incomplete, and 80% increase for concealed activity or abusive arrangement; late payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month from the original due date. Additional pecuniary penalties of up to EUR 15,000 may apply for recurrence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% under domestic law (Article 119 bis CGI) on gross dividends paid by a French SAS to non-resident corporate shareholders; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the EU/EEA parent meets the ≥10% holding and two-year holding period; treaty rates commonly 0%, 5% or 15% depending on percentage of capital held.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must (i) be the beneficial owner, (ii) submit to the French paying entity a valid tax residence certificate (Formulaire 5000 / attestation de résidence fiscale) before the payment date, and (iii) provide supporting proof of shareholding and holding period. If domestic WHT has been applied, a refund claim must be filed with the DGFiP (SIE – Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères) using the applicable claim forms before the statutory limitation period of 31 December of the second year following the year of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax 33.33% under Article 182 B CGI on payments for the use of industrial, commercial, or intellectual property; treaty rates are frequently 0% or 5% for the beneficial owner. Interest: French domestic law generally imposes no withholding tax on arm's-length interest paid to non-residents on commercial debts or bonds, except in certain tax-haven situations; treaty rates normally range from 0% to 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation applies where the French entity belongs to a group whose consolidated annual turnover or gross assets exceed EUR 400 million (Article L.13 AA LPF). Members of such a group must prepare and file a Master File and a French Local File. Entities with fewer than 250 employees and either turnover not exceeding EUR 50 million or total assets not exceeding EUR 43 million are ordinarily exempt from formal documentation obligations unless transacting with non-cooperative jurisdictions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substance requirements are embedded in the French General Anti-Abuse Rule (abus de droit, Article L.64 LPF), the 'acte anormal de gestion' doctrine, and the OECD BEPS minimum standards. A French SAS must evidence real local substance: actual premises, employees, local management and business decisions. A pure letterbox company or an intermediary with no economic function is exposed to recharacterisation, profit adjustment, and anti-avoidance penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of turnover, artificial inflation of costs, or concealment of French-source taxable activities concerning the collectible trading card business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% to 80% penalty on the underpaid tax plus 0.20% monthly late interest; criminal conviction under Article 1741 CGI carries imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to EUR 500,000, increased to seven years and EUR 750,000 in aggravated circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may be held personally liable for the company's tax debts where fraudulent intent is established; the court may impose a professional ban, a prohibition on managing a French company, travel bans (interdiction du territoire français), and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or using a nominal SAS with no real commercial substance, controlled from abroad, solely to secure tax advantages or treaty benefits under the parent-subsidiary regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French tax administration may disregard the artificial entity, recharacterise the transactions, reassess income at the level of the real taxpayer, and impose an 80% penalty for abuse of law in cases of fraud or sham, together with late interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur 'action en comblement du passif' under Article L.651-2 of the Commercial Code if the shell's insolvency results from their mismanagement; criminal liability for tax evasion may also be asserted personally, with potential imprisonment and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Disclosure / Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border payments for royalties, licences, or service fees at non-arm's-length prices, or failure to file the required transfer pricing documentation, including the Master File and Local File, after the statutory 30-day notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of EUR 30,000 for non-communication of the documentation, plus a surcharge of 5% of the undocumented transactions; reassessment of taxable profits at arm's length and an additional 40% penalty for bad-faith withholding of documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the distorted pricing may be jointly liable for the corporate tax arrears and penalties in cases of intentional fault; criminal prosecution for tax evasion may lead to personal fines and disqualification from management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or keep up to date the beneficial ownership declaration of the SAS with the French commercial registry (RCS / INPI), or use of the company to launder funds through fictitious trading card sales using Stripe or other payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine for the company and criminal fines for the president or manager; failure to declare beneficial owners can trigger a fine of up to EUR 15,000 and imprisonment of up to six months; anti-money laundering violations may attract additional penalties under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for failure to rectify the beneficial ownership register; in severe money laundering cases, travel bans and imprisonment up to five years are possible, and the court may order the company to be wound up or the director to be barred from managing any French business.
